record.original_question: Suppose x is a nicely defined cardinal invariant such that x = ℵ1 already forces the failure of the strong polarized relation \( inom{x}{\omega} 	o  inom{x}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\), meaning there is a 2-coloring of x×ω with no monochromatic rectangle A×B satisfying |A| = x and |B| = ω. Must it follow that x is the continuum c?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Suppose x is a nicely defined invariant which satisfies x = ℵ1 ⇒ (x over ω) ↛ (x over ω)^(1,1)_2. Does it follow that x = c?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that for cardinals $\kappa$ and $\lambda$, the strong polarized partition relation $\binom{\kappa}{\lambda} \to \binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2$ asserts that for every coloring $c\colon \kappa \times \lambda \to 2$ there exist sets $A \subseteq \kappa$ with $|A| = \kappa$ and $B \subseteq \lambda$ with $|B| = \lambda$ such that $c$ is constant on $A \times B$. The negation $\binom{\kappa}{\lambda} \not\to \binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2$ means there is a 2-coloring of $\kappa \times \lambda$ admitting no such monochromatic rectangle.

Let $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$ denote the continuum, and consider cardinal invariants of the continuum $\mathfrak{x}$ (i.e., cardinals satisfying $\aleph_1 \le \mathfrak{x} \le \mathfrak{c}$, definable in a sufficiently absolute way) such as $\mathfrak{b}$, $\mathfrak{d}$, $\mathfrak{p}$, $\mathfrak{t}$, $\mathfrak{s}$, $\mathfrak{a}$, $\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{M})$, etc.

Question: Suppose $\mathfrak{x}$ is such a (nicely defined) cardinal invariant of the continuum with the property that, in every model of ZFC in which $\mathfrak{x} = \aleph_1$, the strong polarized relation fails, i.e.,
$$\mathfrak{x} = \aleph_1 \;\Longrightarrow\; \binom{\mathfrak{x}}{\omega} \not\to \binom{\mathfrak{x}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2.$$
Must it then be provable in ZFC that $\mathfrak{x} = \mathfrak{c}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem by Garti and Shelah in their work on partition calculus and cardinal invariants. A follow-up paper "Open and solved problems concerning polarized partition relations" (Fund. Math. 234, 2016) addresses several such problems, but no clear statement was found in the search confirming that this specific problem ("does the negative strong polarized relation at ℵ₁ characterize being equal to the continuum among nicely defined invariants?") has been resolved. Status appears to be unknown from the available search evidence.

status_evidence.title: Partition Calculus and Cardinal Invariants (arXiv:1112.5772)
status_evidence.snippet: Garti–Shelah investigation of which cardinal invariants $\mathfrak{x}$ satisfy the strong polarized relation, with problems posed about when $\mathfrak{x}=\aleph_1$ forces failure.
status_evidence.claim: Problem of the form considered here is posed in Garti–Shelah's work on partition calculus and cardinal invariants.

status_evidence.title: Open and solved problems concerning polarized partition relations (Fund. Math. 234, 2016)
status_evidence.snippet: Garti and Shelah list which polarized-partition problems have been solved and which remain open.
status_evidence.claim: A later survey by the same authors enumerates open and solved problems in this area, but did not surface a definitive resolution of this specific problem in the search.
